ambiguity_expected_states.rationale: Every apparent weight variation for a similarly-named criterion (Corporate Profile: 5/5/10; Key Personnel and Roster: 15/15/20) is scoped to a distinct, explicitly-named category (Appendix D1/D2/D3) in the same source table. No occurrence of the same criterion label with a different value WITHIN the same category/scope was found anywhere in the 16-document corpus. The historical Deep-derived report's claimed third 'Key Personnel: 100 points' value is, in the source text, Category 3's own 'Total points: 100 points' row -- not a Key Personnel value. The historical claimed 'Methodology: 5 points' value does not appear anywhere in the corpus at all; the 30 and 35-point figures Deep cites belong to two DIFFERENTLY-NAMED criteria ('Facilitation Methodology' in D3, 'Methodology and Advisory Approach' in D2), not one repeated label.

Category 3's own rated-criteria table scores 'Price' as a 25-point line item (page 16), while section 3.1 separately defines 'Stage 4. Pricing' as its own evaluation stage applied to every qualified proposal (page 9). A bidder in Category 3 cannot tell from the RFP alone whether this means price is scored once (via the embedded line item) or twice (there, and again at Stage 4). This is a genuine, source-supported structural ambiguity, not a conflation.

Category 1 and Category 3 each have their own, distinctly-dated presentation stage ('Week of October 26' and 'Week of November 2' respectively), sharing the same underlying milestone label (Presentation/Demonstration). This is best described as a scoped, category-specific difference rather than a contradiction -- a bid team tracking only one date could still miss the one applicable to its own category, so it is worth surfacing, but it is not evidence of an internally inconsistent RFP the way a same-scope value conflict would be.
